title: Dictator versus no notable coordinates
statement: For every $\delta\in(0,1/2)$, there is a family of finite-seed sign testers using three-variable linear sign predicates, with thresholds $\alpha=1/2$ and $\beta=1-\delta$, and error function $E_{2\delta}(\varepsilon)$, where $E_r(\varepsilon)=\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ if $\varepsilon\le r$ and $1/2$ otherwise. The predicate set is finite; the error maps $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$ and tends to zero as $\varepsilon$ approaches zero through positive values. Every test uses an allowed predicate, every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, and every function whose stable influences at parameters $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha+E_{2\delta}(\varepsilon)$, for every dimension, every positive dimension, and every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
hypotheses_covered: The error tends to zero at zero through positive arguments
Every test uses a predicate from the specified set
Every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$
Every function with all stable influences at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha$ plus the error, for $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$
The assertions hold in every positive dimension
